summaries.text: Backend engineer with six years building services that stay up: cut p99 latency 60% on a 4B-request/month API, and led the migration off a monolith without a customer-visible incident. Comfortable owning a system end to end, from schema design to on-call.

Data platform engineer who has run streaming infrastructure at production scale — 1.2M events/sec through Kafka with exactly-once delivery — and built the self-serve tooling that let 40 analysts ship pipelines without filing tickets.

Engineer shipping LLM features in production, from a retrieval service answering 200k support questions a month to an internal agent framework now used by four product teams. Backend depth plus hands-on experience with evaluation, cost control, and latency budgets.

bullets.text: Cut p99 latency 60% on a 4B-request/month routing API by replacing synchronous fan-out with a cached materialized view.
Led the decomposition of a 400k-line monolith into eight services, shipping incrementally with zero customer-visible downtime.
Built the on-call runbook and tracing standards now used by every backend team, cutting mean time to resolution from 90 to 22 minutes.
Shipped an internal agent framework on top of the Claude API that four product teams now use for support triage and document extraction.
Scaled a Kafka pipeline from 80k to 1.2M events/sec with exactly-once delivery, absorbing a 15x traffic increase without adding headcount.
Built a self-serve pipeline framework in Python that let 40 analysts ship transformations without engineering review, eliminating a two-week queue.
Reduced Snowflake spend 38% by rewriting the ten costliest models in dbt with incremental materialization.
Built the public REST API and its client SDKs, onboarding the first 120 integration partners.
Automated the release pipeline, taking deploys from weekly and manual to twelve a day.
